title: Cluster discovery, tagging, and health signals — playground notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick notes + experiment log for a lightweight, multi-region cluster discovery and inventory approach that combines static labels, ephemeral attestation tags, and health signal scoring to enable smarter routing policies for the inference control plane. Intended as a working doc to collect tradeoffs and small reference implementations before we formalize into a design doc or playbook.

Context / constraints:
- Multi-region: we operate 3 active regions (us-west, eu-central, ap-southeast) with inter-region fallbacks.
- Workloads: mix of low-latency (real-time chat) and high-throughput batch (embeddings), and model variants with different quantizations.
- Hardware diversity: A100/AE, H100, and smaller T4/V100 pools; some nodes have mixed GPUs (2xA100+1xT4).
- Security: control-plane runs in VPC peered networks for private deploys; inventory must be auditable.

Goals:
- Make routing decisions based on real-time capacity, GPU type/quantization support, and node health score.
- Keep discovery light-weight; avoid flipping expensive consistent-store traffic on every heartbeat.
- Support rollouts that pin models to GPU capabilities (e.g., BF16/INT8 vs int4 quantized kernels).
- Provide visibility for operators: topology, capacity buckets, and degradation triggers.

Core concepts (sketch):
1) Node identity + static labels:
   - Each node has a long-lived identity (UUID) and a set of static labels populated at boot/registration: region, zone, rack-id (if available), instance-type, host-gpu-types (list).
   - Examples: region=us-west2, zone=us-west2-a, host-gpu-types=[h100,a100], locality=zone, on_prem=true
2) Attestation / ephemeral tags:
   - Short-lived tags issued after node attestation and health checks: available_for_workloads=true/false, maintenance_window=true, degraded_io=true
   - Tags TTL: default 30s - 120s depending on heartbeat frequency. Tags stored in inventory cache with vector of (tag, expiry, weight).
3) Health signals + composite health score:
   - Multiple signals: kernel/device driver version, GPU ECC errors, temperature spike, PCIe errors, nvlink state, memory pressure, container runtime watchdogs, process watchdogs for inference runtime.
   - Each signal mapped to a numeric penalty; health_score = 100 - sum(penalties) normalized to 0-100.
   - Health_score categories: healthy(>90), degraded(60-90), critical(<60).
   - Signals are both immediate (thermal spike) and aggregated (15m rolling error rate).
4) Capacity scoring and fractional GPU availability:
   - For mixed nodes, expose fractional capacity per GPU type. Example: NodeA has 2xA100 and 1xT4 → capacity map {a100:2, t4:1}.
   - Batching-aware capacity: some workloads benefit from concurrency (batching) and others from dedicated low-latency. Add a concurrency_score that describes expected QPS for given model+sequence length.
5) TTL + reconciliation model:
   - Nodes push heartbeat every 20s; control plane keeps last_seen timestamp and TTL=heartbeat_interval*3. Expire node labels/tags after TTL.
   - For multi-region control-plane federation, we maintain a per-region inventory and an asynchronously replicated global index with eventual consistency. Routing can use local region inventory + global fallback.
6) Discovery API surfaces:
   - /inventory/query?region=us-west2&gpu=a100&min_health=80&cap_type=low_latency
   - /inventory/watch?route=chat-low-latency - websocket/stream of delta updates (added/removed node ids with tags)

Routing policy examples:
- Latency-first route: prefer nodes in same region and zone with health_score>90 and gpu_type matching model kernel; if none, fall back to same region different zone; then cross-region fallback with degraded concurrency caps.
- Cost-aware route: prefer nodes tagged as preemptible or burst and with quantized kernels (int4) with health_score>75 for batch workloads.
- Canary rollout: send 5% of traffic to nodes with model_variant=v2 and gpu_support=bf16; monitor error_rate and latency; auto rollback threshold = 2.5x baseline error or 20% p99 increase.

Inventory storage choices explored:
- Option A: Centralized RDS-backed inventory with an in-memory cache per control-plane instance. Pros: simple queries, ACID for writes. Cons: cross-region latency, single write path.
- Option B: Region-local ephemeral stores (Redis) with async global index via Kafka topics. Pros: local reads fast, independent regional failure modes. Cons: eventual consistency, slightly more complex reconciliation.
- Option C: CRDT-based gossip inventory (per-region) with per-node tombstones. Pros: fully distributed; Cons: complexity, heavier on metadata churn.
Recommendation (current lean): Start with Option B. Use region-local Redis for fast reads/watches; publish node events to Kafka for global index/analytics. Keep tombstones compact and TTLed.

Health telemetry pipeline notes:
- Device plugin: expose per-GPU counters, nvml snapshots (~every 10s). Normalize signals into a small vector.
- Aggregation: rollup to 1m and 15m windows for steady-state error rates. Keep raw 10s resolution for critical alerts for a short retention (24h).
- Alerting: health_score<60 emits pager, persistent ECC errors -> investigate; thermal spikes -> soft throttle/evacuate model containers.

Operational playbook snippets:
- Node enters degraded_io state (score drop 15+ in 5m): mark available_for_workloads=false for latency routes, keep for batch if capacity allows. Notify SRE channel.
- Node heartbeat missing 3x: mark TTL expired, start eviction scoreboard and re-route inflight requests.
- Planned maintenance: operator sets maintenance_window=true with expected_duration; scheduler drains new traffic but leaves longer-running batch to complete.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- How to represent kernel/driver compat matrix succinctly for model kernel selection? (Proposal: feature flags in static labels e.g. supports-int4-kernels=true)
- Should we weight recent transient signals more heavily than older errors? (we currently propose exponential decay on penalties)
- How to surface GPU memory fragmentation (allocatable vs total) without heavy telemetry cost? (approx sampling + periodic full reports)
- Circuit breaker for global index staleness: define SLA window where global inventory is considered stale for routing decisions.

Prototype tasks:
- [ ] Implement region-local Redis schema (key format: inventory:region:{region}:node:{node_id} -> JSON blob). Keep blob small (~1KB).
- [ ] Kafka topic node-events.{region} with compacted keys for node_id; write producers in node agent; consumer builds global index for analytics.
- [ ] Small HTTP service /inventory/query and /inventory/watch backed by Redis pubsub for delta streaming.
- [ ] Basic health scoring lib (python/golang) with pluggable signals and configurable weights.

Notes / references:
- Related GH PRs: platform/pull/678 (node agent attestation), platform/pull/701 (gpu telemetry shim)
- Slack: #infra-arch thread 2025-01-23 (attestation mini-proposal)
- Related Confluence: Cluster Inventory Home (link above)

Quick mental model summary (one-liner):
Keep static labels for durable characteristics (region, gpu types, topology), ephemeral tags for availability/maintenance, and a compact health_score to drive routing decisions. Use region-local stores for low-latency discovery and an async global index for analytics and cross-region fallback.

Unresolved: final TTLs, telemetry retention, exact schema for fractional GPU capacity. Will iterate after prototype runs for 2 weeks.

Last experiment log (2025-03-28):
- Deployed prototype in us-west2 with Redis+Kafka. Observed median /inventory/query latency 12ms (cold miss 28ms).
- Health scoring produced too many transient degraded states when thermal spikes lasted <10s. Plan: add debounce (3s) and bump exponential decay window.

Feedback welcome — ping @priya in #infra-arch or add notes here.
